clue.text: Naughty nude lay outside party with no sense of shame

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit outside the party word, wrapping round it
naughty behaviour is disorderly, so the letters of nude lay are rearranged

parts.note: a bash is a party

explanation.surface: Someone sunbathing naked at a party shows no embarrassment at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' is the anagram signal and 'outside' the container: the shuffled letters split around the party word. 'Party' looks like the definition's company but is a slang synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unashamedly means doing it brazenly, without embarrassment.

clue.text: Some fine area not a million miles away

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pleasant neighbourhood that is quite close by.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'not a million miles away' means close at hand.

clue.text: Large place in Kent? I don't think it's that wonderful!

definitions.text: I don't think it's that wonderful!

parts.note: big means large
Deal is a seaside town in Kent, a county in south-east England

explanation.surface: Someone unimpressed by a large Kentish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Said sarcastically, the exclamation dismisses something as unimpressive.

clue.text: Member of family admits love willingly

indicators.note: admitting lets the zero letter in, inside the family member

parts.note: a son is a family member
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A relative readily confesses to being in love.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'I'd as soon stay', the word can mean readily or willingly.

clue.text: Start of evening and sloppy seat is most comfortable

indicators.note: takes only the first letter of evening
sloppy means careless and untidy, so the letters of seat is are jumbled

explanation.surface: At dusk, a slouchy chair is the comfiest.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of easy can mean the most relaxed or comfortable.

clue.text: See commercial notice giving charge

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: An advert announcing a price.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is a burden or quantity carried, as in loading a gun or a cart.

clue.text: Grand spot — it will be redeveloped for a store

indicators.note: redevelopment rebuilds, so the letters of grand spot and it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prime site is to be rebuilt as a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier store where goods were bartered, especially with fur trappers.

clue.text: John in Scotland, after pain and deprivation, is naively optimistic

indicators.note: the Scottish name is placed after the other two pieces

parts.note: a pang is a sudden sharp pain
loss is a deprivation of something
Ian is the Scottish form of the name John

explanation.surface: A Scotsman stays cheerful despite suffering and hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Pangloss, in Voltaire's Candide, insists all is for the best in the best of all possible worlds.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective comes from Voltaire's relentlessly hopeful tutor, so it describes blind, unrealistic cheerfulness.

clue.text: Treat person in trouble, offering a lift

indicators.note: something in trouble is disordered, so the letters of treat person are rearranged

explanation.surface: Helping a struggling person by giving them a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A continuously moving chain of open lift cars is called a paternoster lift.

clue.text: Don't give up — and don't tell someone else to give up?

definitions.text: don't tell someone else to give up?
definitions.meaning: read literally, an instruction never to utter the word 'die', that is, to tell someone to quit

explanation.surface: Advice to persevere and not to discourage others.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a rallying cry to persevere, and literally an order never to speak a word that urges surrender.

clue.text: Doris has her newly prepared sauce

indicators.note: preparing afresh reorders the letters of Doris has her

explanation.surface: Doris has made her own fresh condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent root condiment, traditionally served with roast beef.

clue.text: Bring up what is brought up last

explanation.surface: A play on two senses of bringing up.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is raising a family; the other is the hindmost part, as in the phrase bringing up the rear.

clue.text: Nameless devil in short protest

indicators.note: without a name means the letter N, standard for name, is dropped

parts.note: a demon is a devil

explanation.surface: An anonymous troublemaker joins a brief demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: N is a common abbreviation for name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a clipped form of demonstration, a public protest march.

clue.text: Chaperons expected when two knights enter

indicators.note: the two knights go into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: due means expected, as a train is due
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
N is the chess abbreviation for knight, so two give NN

explanation.surface: Chaperones arrive on time just as a pair of knights turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman who accompanies and supervises young girls, especially in Spain.

clue.text: An old-fashioned thing that could get one carried away

definitions.text: An old-fashioned thing that could get one carried away

parts.words: An old-fashioned thing that could get one carried away
parts.note: carried away is literal: an enclosed chair borne on poles by two porters

explanation.surface: Something dated that might excite a person too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair was a covered seat carried on poles, used in the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: Birds and what they catch when aboard old ship

indicators.note: going aboard places one piece inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
prey is what hunting birds catch

explanation.surface: Fishing birds land on an old vessel with their catch.
explanation.definitionFit: These are large fish-eating raptors, also called sea hawks.

clue.text: Tipsy but well able to move around?

explanation.surface: A slightly drunk person who can still get about.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-oiled is slang for drunk; lubricated machinery moves smoothly.

clue.text: It's within the law to hurry on foot

definitions.meaning: the slang phrase '...' means run off

explanation.surface: Running away is apparently quite lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: It is slang for lawful or genuine; split in two it gives the British slang for running away.

clue.text: Hour of prayer for nobody

definitions.meaning: the monastic office said at the ninth hour, mid-afternoon

explanation.surface: No one turns up to the afternoon service.
explanation.definitionFit: Nones is the ninth-hour office in church liturgy; the everyday word means not any person.

clue.text: That's a ruler — the ruler hiding there!

indicators.note: points back to the words before the dash, which conceal the answer across their joins

explanation.surface: Someone points out a monarch concealed nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of That's, the word a and the start of ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian emperor was the absolute ruler of the country before 1917.

clue.text: Challenges are embraced by daughter and son

indicators.note: embraced means held inside, so the word are sits between the two letters

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A family's children are being hugged and dared.
explanation.definitionFit: To dare someone is to challenge them to do something bold; the plural noun fits too.

clue.text: Cloth suffices, sort without hem

parts.note: does means is enough, as in 'that does'

indicators.note: a hem is an edge, so the edge letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: kind means sort or type

explanation.surface: A tailor says this fabric will do, unhemmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Doeskin is a fine soft woollen fabric with a smooth finish, as well as leather.

clue.text: Ordered last of woodsmen into wild forest

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the scrambled forest
wild means untamed, so the letters of forest are scrambled
takes the final letter of woodsmen

explanation.surface: A lumberjack was summoned into untamed woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: To have sent for something is to have ordered or summoned it.

clue.text: Permit one operating to show high emotion

parts.note: a pass is a permit
I is the Roman numeral one
on means working or operating, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: An official gives permission for someone to display strong feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Passion is intense, overwhelming feeling such as love or anger.

clue.text: Held up legal document that contains poem

indicators.note: the document holds the poem inside it

parts.note: a deed is a signed legal document
a lay is a short narrative poem or song

explanation.surface: A contract with verse in it was stalled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held up means being made late or kept waiting.

clue.text: Check part of plant

definitions.meaning: to stop or stanch a flow
the main stalk of a plant

explanation.surface: Inspect a section of greenery, or a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem bleeding is to check it; the stalk of a plant carries the same name.

clue.text: Thirty-one days round part of the Emerald Isle

parts.note: May is a month with 31 days
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A month's tour around a region of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is a county in the west of Ireland, the island nicknamed for its green landscape.

clue.text: Money put down had to include note

indicators.note: the eating word takes the note letter inside it

parts.note: had, as in had a meal, means ate

explanation.surface: A cash deposit had to cover a banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker, the stake placed before dealing is money staked in advance.

clue.text: Gentlemen in states of agitation when losing time

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: stirs are commotions or flurries of excitement

explanation.surface: Men become flustered as time runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the formal plural form of address for men, as in a letter's opening.

clue.text: Lose rotten fruit

indicators.note: rotten means decayed, so the letters of lose are rearranged

explanation.surface: Throw away fruit that has gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackthorn bears a small sour blue-black berry used in gin.

clue.text: Common soldiers row one way and another

parts.note: a rank is a line running side by side
a file is a line running front to back, the other way

explanation.surface: Ordinary troops quarrel back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: In a military formation, ranks run across and files run from front to back; 'row' might suggest a quarrel but means a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means ordinary troops as opposed to officers, and by extension ordinary members.

clue.text: Nasty death drew on, making one dejected

indicators.note: a nasty turn of events reshuffles the letters of death drew on

explanation.surface: An unpleasant end approached, leaving someone low.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe being in low spirits and discouraged.
